claims.text: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered single-phase BCC alloy in the as-cast state.
As-cast equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of approximately 1719 MPa.
As-cast equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has limited plasticity.
The high Mo content increases the electronegativity difference in NbZrTiHfMo.
The increased electronegativity difference associated with high Mo content contributes to reduced plasticity.
An approximately 80% cold reduction followed by annealing near 750°C for 20 minutes will improve the room-temperature compressive strength–plasticity balance of equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo.
Heavy cold rolling increases dislocation density and produces dislocation tangles in the alloy.
Heavy cold rolling produces elongated microstructural features, low- or medium-angle boundaries, and strong texture.
The rolling-induced dislocation structures and boundaries impede dislocation motion and increase strength through work hardening.
Annealing at approximately 750°C for 20 minutes causes partial recovery and partial recrystallization in heavily rolled NbZrTiHfMo.
Partial recovery and recrystallization reduce localized stress concentrations and dislocation heterogeneity.
Reducing stress concentrations and dislocation heterogeneity facilitates more uniform slip and improves plasticity.
Annealing below 800°C avoids full recrystallization while retaining most of the dislocation-based strengthening.
The proposed treatment must preserve the single-phase BCC structure for the beneficial effect to occur.
The treated alloy will retain comparable compressive yield strength, with a decrease of less than approximately 10%.
The treated alloy may exhibit approximately 50% greater ductility than the 80%-rolled, unannealed condition.
The 80%-rolled, unannealed alloy has high strength but limited plasticity.
Annealing beyond the proposed temperature or time limits may cause excessive recrystallization and grain growth.
Excessive recrystallization and grain growth would cause a marked loss of strength.
